tasks.short: Update emergency response plans and procedures.

steps.what: Read the current emergency response plan and procedures.
Note on site which emergency procedures no longer match.
Draft updated emergency procedures from her site notes.

loop.purpose: Turn her site notes into procedure sentences.
loop.input: A site note naming an exit, an assembly point, or a role.
loop.output: A draft procedure sentence tied to that note.
loop.check: Each sentence names an exit, assembly point, or role that her note already states.
loop.stop: A sentence has no matching note, or she rejects the draft.
loop.why_not_simpler: The notes are free text, so a fixed template cannot write the sentence.

steps.what: Check each procedure against the site note it cites.
Accept the emergency plan version that matches the site.
File the accepted emergency response plan.

tasks.design: She still walks the site and writes the notes. A draft in the {DOCS} only restates those notes, and she checks that each procedure names an exit, assembly point, or role from a note. Filing the accepted plan is its own step. Nothing is sent outside, and no alert goes out.
tasks.previous_blocker: The plan was a long document rewritten once a year from memory.
tasks.enabler_now: Her site notes can be fields a draft must cite.
tasks.still_hard: A layout change with no note still needs her walk.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a blocked exit that the old plan still calls clear.

ambition.what: She updates the assembly point when a site note says it moved, instead of waiting for the yearly rewrite.

tasks.altitude: She still owns which procedure changes. The plan is filed only after she accepts that version.

reach.task: Walk the evacuation route and note a blocked exit.
reach.learn: Which note fields the procedure draft is allowed to use.

evidence.claim: LabSafety Bench found no model passed 70 percent accuracy at hazard identification.
Arbo rules need works council consent under WOR art. 27(1)(d).
A draft can restate notes she already wrote, and she still has to check the meaning. Model knowledge, E1.

assumptions: A site note has location, what is wrong, an exit or assembly point, and a responsible role. She writes it in s2. If a note lacks those fields, s3 does not run and she writes the procedure in s5.
s6 files only the plan version she accepted in s5. An edit after that acceptance voids the file.
This task does not send the plan outside the organisation.
unknowns: Whether the works council treats each emergency-plan edit as an arbo-rule change.
research_questions: Does a plan edit go to the works council before s6 files it?

already_counted.description: She checks each drafted sentence against the site note.

incremental.description: She rewrites a sentence that cited a note but changed the exit or the role.

approvals.approved_version: emergency plan she accepted in s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a year when the layout changed and her notes do not name the new exit, so the draft does not run. High is a year when only names and assembly points changed and every sentence matched a note.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Coordinate right-to-know programs for hazardous substances.

steps.what: Collect supplier sheets for hazardous chemicals on site.
Extract hazard and first-aid lines from each sheet.

loop.purpose: Read the hazard and first-aid lines out of a supplier sheet.
loop.input: The text of a supplier safety data sheet.
loop.output: A hazard sentence and a first-aid sentence.
loop.check: Both sentences appear in the sheet, not only a substance number.
loop.stop: A sentence is missing from the sheet, or the sheet has no text.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier sheets are unstructured, so a field map cannot read them.

steps.what: Check each hazard line against the sheet wording.
Decide which hazardous substances the program includes.
File the accepted hazardous substance list.
Brief team leads on the hazardous substances they handle.

tasks.design: A reading step pulls the hazard and first-aid sentences from the supplier sheet into a draft. She checks those sentences against the sheet, then decides the list. Filing that accepted list is its own step. She briefs team leads in person from the filed list. That talk is not a send, and no mail goes out.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sheets sat in a folder and the substance list was retyped.
tasks.enabler_now: A reader can propose hazard lines that a person checks against the sheet before the list is filed.
tasks.still_hard: A scanned sheet with no text still needs her to read it.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which crew actually handles a substance the sheet only names.

ambition.what: She adds a substance the week its sheet is checked, instead of at the yearly program review.

tasks.altitude: She still decides the list and still briefs the crews in person.

reach.task: Name the handling line on a substance they use.
reach.learn: How a checked hazard line reaches the crew brief.

evidence.claim: EcoOnline SDS Smart Extraction reads supplier safety data sheets, and a person reviews them before records are created.
Arbo rules need works council consent under WOR art. 27(1)(d).
She still decides which substances a crew must be told about. Model knowledge, E1.

assumptions: The sheet fields are substance name, hazard sentence, first-aid sentence, handling sentence, and revision date. The supplier produces the sheet. If the sheet has no text, s2 does not run and she types the lines in s3.
s5 files only the list she accepted in s4. An edit after that acceptance voids the file.
The brief in s6 is a talk with team leads inside the organisation. It is not a send.
unknowns: What share of supplier sheets arrive as text rather than as a scan.
research_questions: Which sheets this year have no text layer for the reader to use?

already_counted.description: She checks each extracted line against the sheet wording.

incremental.description: She corrects a hazard line that quoted the sheet but named the wrong handling rule.

approvals.approved_version: hazardous substance list she accepted in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a month of scanned sheets with no text, so extraction does not run. High is a month of repeat sheets whose hazard lines matched the text.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Audit hazardous waste sites and record findings.

steps.what: Walk the hazardous waste site and note handling.
Judge findings against the permit for that waste site.
File the audit findings she confirmed on site.
Tell the site lead which waste findings must change.

tasks.design: She walks the waste site and confirms each finding against the permit. A separate step files only those confirmed findings in the {DOCS}. She then tells the site lead in person. No report is sent to an inspectorate, and no alert goes out.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings lived in a notebook and were copied later by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: A finding she has already worded can be copied into the action list without a new draft.
tasks.still_hard: Judging storage and a leak still happens on site.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a container the permit allows but the store cannot hold safely.
tasks.altitude: The walk and the judgement stay hers. Only the confirmed wording is copied.

reach.role: Environmental Science and Protection Technicians, Including Health
reach.task: Sample a waste store during the site walk.
reach.learn: Which finding fields she will file.

evidence.claim: The Arbowet requires a written RI&E with an action plan (art. 5), and the arbodienst or company doctor tests the RI&E (art. 14).
Copying finding fields she already confirmed does not judge the site. Model knowledge, E1.

assumptions: A finding has the site, the location, what she saw, and the permit clause. She writes it in s2. If a finding has no permit clause, s3 does not run.
The copy does not add words and does not name a worker. Findings name the place and the rule.
This task does not send a report to the Labour Inspectorate.
unknowns: Whether a finding on this site is ever required to name a person.
research_questions: Which permit clauses are stable enough to store as fields?

already_counted.description: She confirms each finding against the permit before the copy.

incremental.description: She fixes a filed finding that copied the wrong permit clause.

approvals.approved_version: audit findings she confirmed in s2

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is an investigation where findings are not yet tied to a permit clause, so nothing is filed. High is a repeat waste audit where each finding already names a clause.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain medical monitoring programs for employees.

steps.what: Read which roles the medical monitoring program covers.
Note the tests the doctor ties to each exposure.
Fill role, test and interval on the monitoring program.
Check the rows hold tests, not sickness causes.
Accept the medical monitoring program for those roles.
File the accepted medical monitoring program.
Send the accepted program to the arbodienst.

tasks.design: The program names a role, an exposure, a test and an interval. It does not store a diagnosis or a sickness cause, and it does not score a worker. After she accepts it, one step files that version in the {DOCS} and a separate step sends the same version to the arbodienst. A later edit voids both. The meeting with the doctor is a talk, not a send.
tasks.previous_blocker: The program mixed exposure rules with notes about who was ill, and she mailed a fresh copy by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: A fixed row can hold role, test and interval, and the send can wait for that accepted version.
tasks.still_hard: The company doctor still decides whether a person is fit.
tasks.human_edge: Judging that a new agent on a line needs a test the old program never listed.

ambition.what: She adds an exposure group when a new agent appears on a line, instead of at the yearly program review.

tasks.altitude: She still sets the exposure rules with the doctor. She does not hold test results.

reach.task: Schedule the test for an exposure group.
reach.learn: Why the program names a role and a test, not a diagnosis.

evidence.claim: The Dutch data protection authority fined a maintenance firm 15,000 euros for recording the cause of employees' sickness; that belongs with the company doctor.
Monitoring or evaluating workers' behaviour is high-risk AI under Annex III 4(b).
Inferring workers' emotions is prohibited except for medical or safety reasons.
The specialist can keep exposure rules while the doctor holds the results. Model knowledge, E1.

assumptions: A program row is job role, exposure agent, test name, and interval in months. She records the doctor's test names in s2. If a row would hold a diagnosis, a sickness cause, or a named person, s3 does not run.
The arbodienst is outside the organisation. s6 files and s7 sends only the version she accepted in s5. An edit after that acceptance voids both.
Test results stay with the company doctor. This task does not record them. The meeting in s2 is a talk, not a send.
unknowns: Whether this firm's doctor is employed inside, in which case the program would not be sent outside.
research_questions: Does the arbodienst accept the program only by mail?

already_counted.description: She checks that rows name a role and a test, not a diagnosis.

incremental.description: She removes a row that named a person or a sickness cause before the file or the send.

approvals.approved_version: monitoring program she accepted in s5
monitoring program she accepted in s5

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low is a year when exposures changed and she rewrote the rules with the doctor, so the fill and the send do not run. High is a year when only intervals changed on known roles and she accepted that version.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still walks sites, judges hazards, and briefs colleagues. A plan, a substance list, an audit finding, or a monitoring program is filed only after she accepts that version. Only the monitoring program is sent outside.
